name: A Rod Keeping Hours
description: A single thin rod of warm neon hangs in an autumn dusk, casting a soft fan of light onto the wall below, and along its upper edge it quietly notches every hour of music the house has heard today.
listening: The bass breathes the rod a little longer, rising tension narrows and gathers its fan, treble thins the haze into a fine grain, the key leans the glow between rust and apricot, each song re-angles the fan's skew, the beat only sways it by a hair, and iDay grows one tick per hour so by midnight the rod is a ruler of the day's music.

curator.verdict: A single warm neon line casting a soft fan of rust light onto near-black is exactly the restrained, one-form, one-family piece this wall is for, and the slow tilt reads calmly across the stills. I would hang it, though the promised hour notches are invisible and the fan's gradient is so faint it may band or vanish on a 64x64 LED grid.

post.caption: Today, the house held a quiet stillness, with no music to shape the warm glow of the rod. It hangs steady in the soft autumn dusk, marking time purely by the passing hours themselves, undisturbed and gentle. The light feels like a calm breath, resting softly in the room.
post.alt: A thin horizontal neon rod emits a warm apricot light against a dark wall, with a soft fan of light spreading below it in an autumn dusk setting.
